exercises.instruction: 9, 10, 11, and 12 Verify that the function satisfies the three hypotheses of Rolle’s Theorem on the given interval. Then find all numbers $$c$$ that satisfy the conclusion of Rolle’s Theorem.

problem.paragraph: $$f(x) = 2x^{2} - 4x + 5, \left\lbrack {- 1,3} \right\rbrack$$
$$f(x) = x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 4x + 2, \left\lbrack {- 2,2} \right\rbrack$$
$$f(x) = \sin\left( {x \slash 2} \right), \left\lbrack {\pi \slash 2,3\pi \slash 2} \right\rbrack$$
$$f(x) = x + 1 \slash x, \left\lbrack {\frac{1}{2},2} \right\rbrack$$

Let $$f(x) = 1 - x^{2 \slash 3}$$ . Show that $$f\left( {- 1} \right) = f(1)$$ but there is no number $$c$$ in $$\left( {- 1,1} \right)$$ such that $$f^{\prime}(c) = 0$$ . Why does this not contradict Rolle’s Theorem?
Let $$f(x) = \tan x$$ . Show that $$f(0) = f(\pi)$$ but there is no number $$c$$ in $$\left( {0,\pi} \right)$$ such that $$f^{\prime}(c) = 0$$ . Why does this not contradict Rolle’s Theorem?

exercises.instruction: 19–20 Find the number $$c$$ that satisfies the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem on the given interval. Graph the function, the secant line through the endpoints, and the tangent line at $$\left( {c,f(c)} \right)$$ . Are the secant line and the tangent line parallel?

problem.paragraph: $$f(x) = \sqrt{x}, \left\lbrack {0,4} \right\rbrack$$
$$f(x) = e^{- x}, \left\lbrack {0,2} \right\rbrack$$

Let $$f(x) = \left( {x - 3} \right)^{- 2}$$ . Show that there is no value of $$c$$ in $$\left( {1,4} \right)$$ such that $$f(4) - f(1) = f^{\prime}(c)\left( {4 - 1} \right)$$ . Why does this not contradict the Mean Value Theorem?

Let $$f(x) = 2 - \left| {2x - 1} \right|$$ . Show that there is no value of $$c$$ such that $$f(3) - f(0) = f^{\prime}(c)\left( {3 - 0} \right)$$ . Why does this not contradict the Mean Value Theorem?

exercises.instruction: 23–24 Show that the equation has exactly one real solution.

problem.paragraph: Show that the equation $$x^{3} - 15x + c = 0$$ has at most one solution in the interval $$\left\lbrack {- 2,2} \right\rbrack$$ .
Show that the equation $$x^{4} + 4x + c = 0$$ has at most two real solutions.

list.item: Show that a polynomial of degree $$3$$ has at most three real zeros.
Show that a polynomial of degree $$n$$ has at most $$n$$ real zeros.
Suppose that $$f$$ is differentiable on $$\mathbb{R}$$ and has two zeros. Show that $$f^{\prime}$$ has at least one zero.
Suppose $$f$$ is twice differentiable on $$\mathbb{R}$$ and has three zeros. Show that $$f^{''}$$ has at least one real zero.

problem.paragraph: If $$f(1) = 10$$ and $$f^{\prime}(x) \geqslant 2$$ for $$1 \leqslant x \leqslant 4$$ , how small can $$f(4)$$ possibly be?
Suppose that $$3 \leqslant f^{\prime}(x) \leqslant 5$$ for all values of $$x$$ . Show that $$18 \leqslant f(8) - f(2) \leqslant 30$$ .
Does there exist a function $$f$$ such that $$f(0) = - 1$$ , $$f(2) = 4$$ , and $$f^{\prime}(x) \leqslant 2$$ for all $$x$$ ?

Suppose that $$f$$ and $$g$$ are continuous on $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ and differentiable on $$\left( {a,b} \right)$$ . Suppose also that $$f(a) = g(a)$$ and $$f^{\prime}(x) < g^{\prime}(x)$$ for $$a < x < b$$ . Prove that $$f(b) < g(b)$$ . [Hint: Apply the Mean Value Theorem to the function $$h = f - g$$ .]
Show that $$\sin x < x$$ if $$0 < x < 2\pi$$ .

Suppose $$f$$ is an odd function and is differentiable everywhere. Prove that for every positive number $$b$$ , there exists a number $$c$$ in $$\left( {- b,b} \right)$$ such that $$f^{\prime}(c) = f(b) \slash b$$ .
Use the Mean Value Theorem to prove the inequality
$$\left| \sin a - \sin b \middle| \leqslant \middle| a - b \right| {{for all}a{and}b}$$
If $$f^{\prime}(x) = c$$ ( $$c$$ a constant) for all $$x$$ , use Corollary 7 to show that $$f(x) = cx + d$$ for some constant $$d$$ .
Let $$f(x) = 1 \slash x$$ and
$$g(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{x} & {{if}x > 0} \\ {1 + \frac{1}{x}} & {{if}x < 0} \end{cases}$$
Show that $$f^{\prime}(x) = g^{\prime}(x)$$ for all $$x$$ in their domains. Can we conclude from Corollary 7 that $$f - g$$ is constant?

problem.paragraph: $$\arctan x + \arctan\left( \frac{1}{x} \right) = \frac{\pi}{2},x > 0$$

At 2:00 PM a car’s speedometer reads $$30{mi} \slash h$$ . At 2:10 PM it reads $$50{mi} \slash h$$ . Show that at some time between $$2:00$$ and $$2:10$$ the acceleration is exactly $$120{mi} \slash h^{2}$$ .

Two runners start a race at the same time and finish in a tie. Prove that at some time during the race they have the same speed. [Hint: Consider $$f(t) = g(t) - h(t)$$ , where $$g$$ and $$h$$ are the position functions of the two runners.]
fixed point A number $$a$$ is called a fixed point of a function $$f$$ if $$f(a) = a$$ . Prove that if $$f^{\prime}(x) \neq 1$$ for all real numbers $$x$$ , then $$f$$ has at most one fixed point.

exercises.paragraph: The Mean Value Theorem was first formulated by Joseph-Louis Lagrange (1736–1813), born in Italy of a French father and an Italian mother. He was a child prodigy and became a professor in Turin at the age of 19. Lagrange made great contributions to number theory, theory of functions, theory of equations, and analytical and celestial mechanics. In particular, he applied calculus to the analysis of the stability of the solar system. At the invitation of Frederick the Great, he succeeded Euler at the Berlin Academy and, when Frederick died, Lagrange accepted King Louis XVI’s invitation to Paris, where he was given apartments in the Louvre and became a professor at the Ecole Polytechnique. Despite all the trappings of luxury and fame, he was a kind and quiet man, living only for science.
